notes: Compute-core policy (same principle as nrf5340.json and cxd5602.json): total_sram_bytes reports the figure available to the core that would actually run TFLM, not a partial or ambiguous mix. Here that is the Cortex-M7 -- the higher-performance core with the FPU/DSP throughput ML inference needs, and the practical default for TFLM on this family. Unlike nRF5340's application/network split, STM32H747's SRAM is mostly *shared* between cores: the datasheet's boot-mode section states plainly that the boot memory space may include 'Flash memory and SRAMs (except for ITCM/DTCM RAMs which cannot be accessed by the Cortex-M4 core)' -- meaning only the 192 KB of TCM RAM is M7-exclusive; the remaining 868 KB (512 KB AXI-SRAM + 128+128+32 KB SRAM1-3 + 4 KB backup) is reachable from either core. Because nothing is withheld from the M7, its figure (1060 KB = 1,085,440 B, same itemized-breakdown-over-rounded-headline convention as stm32h743zi.json) equals the identical single-core STM32H743's total exactly. If TFLM is instead hosted on the Cortex-M4 core here, the real budget is smaller: 888,832 B (868 KB) -- the M4 cannot reach the 192 KB TCM. Confirm which core actually hosts TFLM before using this profile if it isn't the M7. total_flash_bytes (2 Mbytes, '2 x 1 Mbyte' dual-bank per the datasheet's own device table) is shared and not core-dependent. st.com blocks automated fetches of this PDF directly; content verified against an Arduino-hosted mirror of the identical document (252 pp., read in full, including the cross-core accessibility sentence quoted above). Dev-kit aliases (Portenta H7, Nicla Vision, OpenMV H7) are the boards commonly associated with this part in the maker ecosystem; their exact board-level part-number match to STM32H747XI specifically (vs. a sibling H747 variant) was not independently re-verified against each board's own schematic in this pass.
